findings.message: Present but unverified: the changed production behaviour in validation-checks.ts (resolveTaskTestFiles, planTaskCheckPlan, smallStandaloneCheckPlan, trivialCheckPlan, runValidationChecks and, through it, runTestFile/reportWithPrinted/testRunEnv/namedResults/unresolvedNote/runOne/tail) is exercised directly by validation-checks.test.ts. That file imports these exports at lines 19-26 and calls them at lines 71-131, 140-202, 225-296, 324-340 and 449+. runValidationChecks is also reached from build-step.test.ts via `runner`. Most of these symbols have an empty testsReaching list, but that is a gap in the graph's grounding for the just-changed file, not missing tests, so no HIGH not-exercised gap is reported. No build record is available, so whether these tests pass cannot be confirmed. Run `npx tsx --test src/mcp/build-step/__tests__/validation-checks.test.ts src/mcp/build-step/__tests__/build-step.test.ts` to confirm they pass before completion.

runTestFile calls mkdtempSync before its try/finally, and nothing catches an error from it. If the temp directory cannot be created (tmp full, EACCES, ENOSPC), the error escapes runTestFile and then runValidationChecks. That breaks runValidationChecks' documented promise that it 'never throws: a spawn failure or timeout is a failed CheckResult with a note'. The validate turn would fail with an exception instead of returning a failed tests check. Fix: wrap the mkdtemp in a try and return a TestFileRun with a note (exitCode null) when it fails, the same way the writeOutput failure is already handled at line 394.

A nested template literal with two inline ternaries joins stdout and stderr, so the separator rule is hard to read. It is also a second, slightly different version of the join in runOne at line 299: that one always adds '\n' before stderr, while this one adds it only when stdout does not already end in a newline. A small shared joinOutput(stdout, stderr) helper would remove both the nesting and the difference.

When the time limit is used up (remainingMs <= 0), the recorded command leaves out the --test-reporter-destination argument, so it does not match what an actual run of that file would execute. This only affects the evidence text, not the verdict.
